title: On Starving through the longest winter
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：starve　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 starve 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the grower ① starved through the longest winter in public, and every buyer in the greenhouse said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three summers on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the grower ② starves through the longest winter in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ starve through the longest winter at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ starved through the longest winter before — a line in the ledger for August 1943 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Starving through the longest winter in public, the grower said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the crate at the far shelf, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ starve the cattle in the upper field in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Starve the cattle in the upper field at once and never mention it again.

By 1956 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the ledger, and a new buyer from the next greenhouse ⑧ starves the cattle in the upper field in public every summer without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the shelf, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ starved through the longest winter again when nobody else would.

⑩ To starve through the longest winter, my mother said in 1961, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the greenhouse remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the greenhouse forgets, somebody starves through the longest winter in silence again and somebody must starve through the longest winter in public all over again.

task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 挨饿（一般过去式 starved through the longest winter：1949 年种植户头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 挨饿（一般现在 starves through the longest winter：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 挨饿（不定式 to starve through the longest winter：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 挨饿（过去完成时 had starved through the longest winter：1943 年八月的收成账上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 挨饿（动名词 starving through the longest winter 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 使挨饿（starve the cattle in the upper field：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去使挨饿让上面那块地的牛挨饿）
G. v. 使挨饿（starve the cattle in the upper field：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 挨饿（后段两处：新来的收购人照例 starves the cattle in the upper field，而母亲又一次 starved through the longest winter）

answers.why: starve 意为“挨饿”，1949 年种植户当着众人面挨饿在最长那个冬天里挨饿，那是大棚里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 starved。
starve 意为“挨饿”，自那以后种植户一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 starves。
starve 意为“挨饿”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯挨饿在最长那个冬天里挨饿”，此处为不定式 to starve through the longest winter。
starve 意为“挨饿”，收成账里 八月 那行字说明早在 1956 年之前就有人挨饿过，故用过去完成时 had starved。
starve 意为“挨饿”，种植户说“挨饿在最长那个冬天里挨饿这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 starving through the longest winter 作主语。
starve 意为“使挨饿”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去使挨饿让上面那块地的牛挨饿”，should ever 之后用原形 starve the cattle in the upper field。
starve 意为“使挨饿”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻使挨饿让上面那块地的牛挨饿（starve the cattle in the upper field at once），以后再也不要提起。
starve 意为“挨饿”，新来的收购人每个夏天都照例使挨饿让上面那块地的牛挨饿，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 starves。
starve 意为“挨饿”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面挨饿在最长那个冬天里挨饿，用一般过去式 starved 叙述。
starve 意为“挨饿”，结尾那句是母亲 1961 年的话：要挨饿在最长那个冬天里挨饿，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和大棚记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 starve 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the grower starved through the longest winter in public, and nobody in the greenhouse forgot it.
Even now the grower starves through the longest winter in silence whenever the greenhouse asks.
Starving through the longest winter in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever starve the cattle in the upper field in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new buyer from the next greenhouse starves the cattle in the upper field in public every summer, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother starved through the longest winter again, and the greenhouse remembered that half.
